title: Annotatio IV §.XIV: Paschal Homily — suffered body vs host; SPIRITUALE CORPUS; pledge and FIGURE
pass_a_gloss: For in this manner one Homily, which is Paschal, instructs the people: There is much difference between the body in which Christ suffered and the body which is consecrated in the host; the body indeed in which Christ suffered was born from the flesh of the Virgin Mary and consists of blood, bones, skin, nerves and human members and a rational soul; But His SPIRITUAL BODY, which we call the Host, is collected from many grains, without blood, bones, members, without a soul. Further, Christ’s body which once died and rose from death will never afterward die, but is eternal and impassible; but that Host is temporally corruptible, distributed into various parts, finished by teeth and sent into the belly; finally this Mystery is a pledge and FIGURE; Christ’s body is the truth itself.
pass_b_english: Paschal Homily: much difference between the body in which Christ suffered and the body consecrated in the host.

The suffered body has Mary’s flesh, blood, bones, soul; the SPIRITUAL BODY we call Host is from many grains, without blood or soul — temporal, chewable; the Mystery is pledge and FIGURE; Christ’s body is the truth itself.
source_text: Nam hunc in modum Homilia una, quæ Paschalis est, populum instituit: Multum interest inter corpus in quo passus est Christus, & corpus quod in hostia consecratur, corpus quidem in quo Christus passus est, ex Mariæ Virginis carne natum est, ac sanguine, ossibus, cute, nervis & membris humanis atque anima rationali constat; At SPIRITUALE ejus CORPUS, quod Hostiam appellamus, ex multis granis collectum est, sine sanguine, ossibus, membris, sine anima. Deinde Christi corpus quod semel mortuum est & à morte resurrexit, deinceps nunquam morietur, sed æternum est & impassibile, Hostia verò ista temporarie est corruptibilis in varias partes distributa, dentibus confecta & in ventrem transmissa, denique Mysterium hoc, pignus est & FIGURA; Christi corpus est veritas ipsa.
